_comment: Resource trackers. Each card is its own Meld layer at http://127.0.0.1:8790/<id>.html - no query string. EVERY token below was taken from a real Inventory/Lockbox line in Baby's own Palia Assistant logs on 2026-08-19. Never add a guessed token here.
_modes: lifetime = never resets, carries across streams (Amber and Essence only, per Baby 2026-08-16). session = starts at 0 every time she logs into Palia; the previous value is kept for one-click undo. countdown = starts at startAt and counts DOWN as its token is consumed; snaps back to startAt on every server restart (not persisted like the others), per Baby 2026-08-19. A countdown card can also set 'direction' ('gained' or 'lost') to restrict which event type moves it, and 'starOnly': true to only count (1*) star-quality pickups.
_valueBox: Percentages of the card image, measured from the artwork itself by dark+flat detection and checked visually. Re-measure if a card is re-exported.

cards.name: Sashimi
cards._note: UPDATED 2026-09-21: starOnly REMOVED. Since the Palia log bridge went live (see icb-palia-log-bridge.md), this card stopped counting anything - diagnosed by reading the raw game log directly: Palia's own LogInventoryComponent lines only ever carry 'Amount=N ItemType=X', no star/quality marker at all, in any line, for any item (checked broadly, not just this token). The bridge can never produce the '(1*)' marker starOnly requires, so the filter always failed and the countdown froze at startAt. Safe to remove because this card's own original note already established every real Sashimi cook is star-quality anyway ('every real Sashimi cook produces exactly 3 star Sashimi in one line') - starOnly was never excluding any real event for this token, so dropping it changes nothing about which events count, only unfreezes it. Redone 2026-09-06 note below is otherwise unchanged/historical.
cards._note_2026_09_06: Redone 2026-09-06. Baby reported the countdown "did not track the Eldershark" the day before - diagnosed by reading the real log directly (app-20260905.log): the OLD design watched raw 'itemtype_fish_eldershark (1*) lost' lines, but that day's log also had large unrelated Eldershark sell-off/consumption events (x100, x10, x5 batches) that had nothing to do with cooking Sashimi specifically - by the time she actually cooked Sashimi, the pool had long since floored at 0, so it looked broken. Root cause: the tracker was watching the wrong signal (any Eldershark leaving inventory) instead of the actual Sashimi-cooking output. Fixed by switching to the real, directly-verified cooking-output token instead: 'Inventory gained: itemtype_c_sashimi (1*) x3' (verified in app-20260905.log, 19:01 - every real Sashimi cook produces exactly 3 star Sashimi in one line). Now counts down using the same 'count events, not quantity' mechanic as Ramen Plush's 'Ramen Cooked' secondary count (Baby's own words: 'I want it to countdown the way that the Ramen tracker counts up... 1 Sashimi for each 3 I get when I cook a dish... if I cook 1 dish only 1 counts') - server.js's countEvents flag (previously secondary-count-only) was extended to primary countdown cards for this. startAt is 100 per Baby's explicit confirmation ('if we cook 100 then it starts at 100') - 100 cook events = up to 300 actual Sashimi before it hits 0, matching how she thinks about the pool (in cooks, not raw fish or raw dish count). starOnly stays true (only 1-star Sashimi count, same as before). No more token overlap with Fish Stew (which still watches raw itemtype_fish_eldershark) since Sashimi now watches the cooked-output token instead.

cards.name: Fish Stew
cards._note: UPDATED 2026-09-21: starOnly REMOVED. Same bridge limitation as Sashimi (see icb-palia-log-bridge.md and Sashimi's note above) - Palia's raw game log carries no star/quality marker in any LogInventoryComponent line, so starOnly always failed once the bridge became the data source, freezing this countdown. UNLIKE Sashimi, this is not risk-free: this card's own original note says non-star Fish Stew HAS appeared in logs before (e.g. 'itemtype_c_stew_fish x15' with no star marker, likely a restock/resync rather than a real cook) - Baby explicitly chose to fix this anyway, accepting that a non-cook gained-event for this exact token could now decrement the countdown by 1 same as a real cook would, in exchange for the card working again. countEvents:true still means it drops by 1 per matching line regardless of stack size, so this risk is bounded to 'one wrong decrement per stray event', not a wholesale drain. Watch this one if it seems to undercount events that got cooked. Redone 2026-09-09 note below is otherwise unchanged/historical.
cards._note_2026_09_09: Redone 2026-09-09 to match the Sashimi redesign (2026-09-06). Baby: "The fish stew tracker needs to work like the Sashimi tracker and instead of tracking the eldershark being used it should track the fish stew dish being cooked/received. I want it to count down 1 for each time I cook the dish." The OLD design watched raw 'Inventory lost: itemtype_fish_eldershark (1*)' - i.e. ANY star Eldershark leaving inventory for any reason, which is the exact bug that broke Sashimi: bulk fish sell-offs (x100/x30/x10 batches) drained the countdown to 0 long before any real cooking happened. Fixed by watching the real cooking-OUTPUT token instead, verified directly in Baby's own logs (app-20260909.log 02:00-02:07, twelve consecutive real cooks): 'Inventory gained: itemtype_c_stew_fish (1*) x3' - every real Fish Stew cook produces exactly 3 star-quality Fish Stew in one line, identical in shape to Sashimi's cook line. countEvents: true makes it count 1 per cook event regardless of the x3 stack size, per Baby's 'count down 1 for each time I cook the dish'. direction: gained watches the cooking output being received, so selling or eating Fish Stew ('Inventory lost: itemtype_c_stew_fish') never moves the counter. mode countdown + startAt 100 unchanged - server.js makes countdown cards always subtract on their direction-filtered event, so 'gained' still counts DOWN. starOnly: true kept (matches Sashimi; non-star Fish Stew does exist in the logs, e.g. 'itemtype_c_stew_fish x15' with no star marker). tokenOverlapOk REMOVED - that flag only existed because Fish Stew and old-Sashimi both watched the same raw Eldershark token. They no longer overlap at all: Sashimi watches itemtype_c_sashimi, Fish Stew watches itemtype_c_stew_fish, and the two countdowns now move completely independently.

cards.name: Ore vs Kitsuu
cards._note: Built 2026-09-07. Baby dropped 'OreVsKitsuu.png' (1672x941, off-standard canvas like Queen Ushindi/Golden Glory Bee - renderer just scales it) into assets/resources - a single card titled 'Ore vs Kitsuu' with 11 separate blank readout boxes: one under each of 7 ore icons (Jadium, Gold, Iron, Copper, Silver, Palium, Platinum) across the top, and one under each of 4 Kitsuu plush pictures below them (Cave, Obsidian, Caldera, Rainbow). The card's own printed layout groups the ores into 4 mining 'families', each feeding one plush: Jadium alone -> Cave Kitsuu Plush; Gold+Iron -> Obsidian Kitsuu Plush; Copper+Silver -> Caldera Kitsuu Plush; Palium+Platinum -> Rainbow Kitsuu Plush. Baby gave the 4 plush tokens directly; the ore tokens were cross-checked against real log content (Copper/Silver confirmed as genuine tokens via Primary resync lines even though no recent incremental gather event was seen for them in the last 5 days of logs - same 'token is real, just no recent event' situation as Queen Ushindi's slower-moving materials, not a bug). Confirmed with Baby via AskUserQuestion that all 11 boxes should track live numbers, not just the 4 plush counts. This is a LIFETIME, gains-only tracker per Baby's explicit instruction: 'nothing is subtracted when taken out of my inventory, the numbers stack forever and will never be reset' - implemented the same way as Long Tracker, via a top-level `direction: "gained"` field that gates every slot on this card to only count gained events, never lost. Baby also explicitly asked for support up to the millions - the existing slot-card renderer already formats with comma separators (e.g. 1,234,567) but its font-sizing was height-only; extended `renderCollectionCardPage`'s client-side `size()` function to also shrink the font until the number actually fits the box width, since these ore boxes are fairly narrow (~7% of the card width each) and a 7-digit number would have overflowed at the old height-only size. This width-aware shrink applies to every slots-card (Queen Ushindi, Long Tracker too), not just this one - purely additive, only kicks in if a box would otherwise overflow, so it does not change any card that already fit at the height-based size.

cards.name: Bean Burger
cards._note: Built 2026-09-15. Baby: "I also need a Bean Burger counter. Make it to every dish I cook it counts as 1 bean burger prepared." Token 'itemtype_c_beanburger' confirmed two ways: Baby supplied it directly, and it's independently verified in her own live log that same session (app-20260915.log line 45): 'Inventory gained: itemtype_c_beanburger x1' - a real cook right as this was built. Checked 5 days of her other recent logs (app-20260910 through 20260913) and the token only ever appeared in 'Primary gained/lost' resync lines there (not real cook events) until this one - consistent with the house rule that Primary lines are periodic full-inventory snapshots, never counted as deltas. direction:'gained' so eating/selling a Bean Burger ('Inventory lost') never decrements the count - it only ever counts up, same never-resets spirit as Ramen Plush's Plushies count. countEvents:true per Baby's own framing ('every dish I cook... counts as 1') - counts one per real cook line regardless of stack size, same mechanic as Sashimi/Fish Stew/Ramen Cooked, even though the one observed real cook line was already qty 1 (future batched cooks, if any, still count as 1). mode 'lifetime' here just means 'never auto-resets' (not in LIFETIME_SOURCE, so it persists its own count rather than mirroring live.resources - same usage as Ramen Plush's Plushies count), with the existing per-card dashboard +/-/Reset controls available if a manual correction is ever needed. No starOnly filter - the one real cook line observed had no (1*) marker. Card art is Baby's own 'itemtype_c_beanburger.png' (2048x768, dropped directly into assets/resources mid-build) - a cozy purple-and-gold kitchen scene with the blank readout box baked into the art already. Value box re-measured directly from the artwork by dark+flat detection (interior color ~rgb(23,23,31), row/column projection to find the flat rectangle, then checked visually with a red-outline overlay) rather than reusing the house-standard zone, per the project's own 'value boxes are per-skin' rule.

cards.name: Celebration Cake
cards._note: UPDATED 2026-09-21: starOnly REMOVED. Safe to remove: this card's own original note already says 'every real gained/lost line observed for this token carried the (1*) marker' - starOnly was never excluding any real event here, so dropping it changes nothing about which events count, only unfreezes it. Built 2026-09-16 note below is otherwise unchanged/historical.
cards._note_2026_09_16: Built 2026-09-16. Baby: "now I need a celebration cake tracker to countdown from 100." Token 'itemtype_c_dessert_celebrationcake' supplied by Baby along with the card art, dropped directly into assets/resources. This one did NOT fit the usual Sashimi/Fish Stew shape cleanly: real 'Inventory gained' lines for this token are big batches (x30, x60 - looks like restocking/bulk acquisition, not a single cook), and real 'Inventory lost' lines are a mix of single x1 drops (individual gifting/spending) and big batches (x27-30, bulk selling) - watching raw quantity on either direction would risk the exact 'wrong signal drains the pool' bug that broke the old Sashimi/Fish Stew designs. Asked Baby directly via AskUserQuestion rather than guessing which real action should move the countdown; she chose 'count down 1 per cook/batch event (any gained, event-based)' - so direction:'gained' + countEvents:true, same mechanic as Sashimi/Fish Stew/Bean Burger, just applied to a bulk-batch signal instead of a x3 cook line: one 'Inventory gained: itemtype_c_dessert_celebrationcake (1*) xN' line (any N) drops the countdown by exactly 1, never by N. Selling/gifting cakes away ('Inventory lost', x1 or bulk) never touches this countdown, matching her chosen answer. starOnly:true kept - every real gained/lost line observed for this token carried the (1*) marker. mode 'countdown' + startAt 100 per her explicit ask ('countdown from 100'), same snap-back-to-startAt-on-restart behavior as every other countdown card (Sashimi, Fish Stew) - documented, not a bug. Value box re-measured directly from Baby's own art (itemtype_c_dessert_celebrationcake.png, 2048x768, matches house standard) the same way as Bean Burger: dark+flat interior color ~rgb(32,27,38) with a vignette gradient toward the frame, scanned column/row profiles at multiple depths to find the true interior edges (the frame's gold trim starts noticeably outside the flattest-color region), checked visually with a red-outline overlay before finalizing.

cards.name: Giant Goldfish
cards._note: Built 2026-09-17. Baby: "NEED TO TRACK HOW MANY itemtype_fish_giant_goldfish i CATCH." Token confirmed in her own real logs (app-20260916/17.log): real 'Inventory gained' lines are clean, small, one-catch-at-a-time quantities (mostly x1, occasionally x2), some star some not - no bulk-restock or resync noise seen for this token, unlike Celebration Cake/Bean Burger. direction:'gained' so selling/storing goldfish ('Inventory lost') never decrements the catch count - this counts catches, not current holdings. Raw quantity is summed (no countEvents) because there is no fixed per-catch batch size to normalize away - a catch nets 1 or 2 fish and both should count toward 'how many I catch'. No starOnly filter - Baby asked for every catch, not just star-quality ones, and non-star gains were observed in the real log. mode:'session' matches every other raw catch/gather card in this file (Gold Ore, Palium Ore, etc.) - resets each Palia login, same as those. eventSource:'inventory' added defensively (see server.js note by the new eventSource filter) even though this token showed no Lockbox activity in the logs checked - keeps this card's signal source consistent with Eldershark/Mermaid below. Value box measured directly from Baby's own art (giant_goldfish.png, 2048x768) by pixel-profile scanning at the true interior edges (not just the flattest-color core, which undershoots the box on this art due to the vignette), checked visually with a red-outline overlay.

cards.name: Eldershark
cards._note: Built 2026-09-17. Baby: "ALSO MAKE ME A FISHING TRACKER FOR THE itemtype_fish_eldershark." This token needed real investigation before wiring it up (house rule - never guess): its 'Lockbox gained/lost' lines turned out to be periodic full-lockbox-content dumps, not real catch deltas - a single giant line mixing dozens of unrelated housing/decor items together with a fish count, and that fish count repeats the EXACT SAME value many times in a row (e.g. 'itemtype_fish_eldershark (1*) x61' appeared 18 times identically on 2026-09-16, alongside 'x1' also 18 times identically) - the same 'resync mistaken for a delta' bug shape that broke the old Sashimi/Fish Stew designs, just on Lockbox instead of Primary. Added a new opt-in 'eventSource' field to server.js's resourceTrackerScan() specifically to fix this: 'eventSource': 'inventory' restricts a card to only real 'Inventory gained/lost' lines, ignoring Lockbox entirely (every existing card leaves this unset and is unaffected). Real 'Inventory gained' lines for this token are the genuine signal - the large majority observed are clean one-or-two-at-a-time catches (e.g. 78x 'x1' + 12x 'x2' in one day), with one isolated tight-burst cluster of larger identical values (x10/x15, seven lines within 2 seconds on 2026-09-10) that looks like a possible bulk-catch bonus event rather than a bug - left as-is since it's a minority case and the alternative (excluding it) risks under-counting a real bulk catch; worth another look if the count ever looks inflated on a given day. direction:'gained', no starOnly (mixed star/non-star catches are legitimate), no countEvents (raw quantity summed, since a catch's yield varies naturally and there's no fixed batch to normalize away). mode:'session', same convention as every other raw catch/gather card. Value box measured directly from Baby's own art (ELDERSHARK.PNG, 2048x768, 'Legendary Maw' skin) by pixel-profile scanning, checked visually.

Given how little real data exists for this token, worth double-checking the count against Baby's own sense of how many she's caught the first few times it moves. Value box measured directly from Baby's own art (itemtype_fish_inyrevnmermaid.png, 2048x768, 'Mermaid' skin) - this one is noticeably smaller and lower on the card than the other two (the readout sits right under the fish rather than centered in the card), located by pixel-profile scanning, checked visually.

cards._note: Built 2026-09-18. Baby: "Want you to create a highland shark tracker. I will get you the card art." Token confirmed BEFORE the art arrived, straight from a real log line: app-20260917.log, 21:18:59 - 'Inventory gained: itemtype_fish_highlandshark (1*) x1', a genuine starred catch, not a resync line. Only one instance observed so far (small sample - no bulk/resync-shaped noise seen for this token yet, unlike Eldershark's Lockbox dumps). Built the same way as the other fishing-catch cards for consistency: direction:'gained' (selling/storing via 'Inventory lost' never decrements - this counts catches, not current holdings), eventSource:'inventory' (defensive, matches Eldershark/Giant Goldfish/Inyrevn Mermaid even though no Lockbox noise has been seen for this specific token yet), no starOnly (the one observed catch was starred, but nothing says non-star catches shouldn't also count - same reasoning as Giant Goldfish), no countEvents (raw quantity summed - no evidence yet of a fixed per-catch batch size to normalize away). mode:'session' matches every other raw catch/gather card, resets each Palia login. Art supplied by Baby directly in chat: 2048x768 (matches house standard exactly, no resize needed), a moonlit waterfall/lake scene with the shark leaping and a dark navy blank readout panel in a gold frame. Value box measured by dark+flat detection (interior sampled at rgb(21,31,46), restricted to the plausible zone to avoid the art's other dark rock/water shadows), checked visually with a red-outline overlay before finalizing: left 29.20%, top 61.20%, width 41.55%, height 27.60%.

cards.name: Pumpkin Rockhopper Frog vs Plushie
cards._note: Built 2026-10-01. Baby dropped PUMPKIN_ROCKHOPPER_TRACKER.png (2048x768) into assets/resources: one card, two blank boxes labelled FROGS and PLUSHIES. Her instruction: 'track how many of each I pick up and only reset when I manually reset it on the dashboard' - so this is a slots card (never auto-resets; per-slot Reset and Reset-all on control.html), gains only (direction:'gained' - selling/storing never subtracts), Inventory lines only (eventSource:'inventory', ignores Lockbox and Primary resync dumps; slot loop honours eventSource since this build). Tokens verified in real logs (app-bridge-20260930.log): frog = itemtype_bug_az3_hopper_pumpkin (356 caught 2026-09-30/10-01, all 'Inventory gained', x1 or x2 each); plush = itemtype_decor_plush_rockhopper01_pumpkin ('Inventory gained: itemtype_decor_plush_rockhopper01_pumpkin x1' at 2026-10-01 02:43:31). Value boxes measured by dark+flat detection (interior ~rgb(24,40,30)) and checked with a red-outline overlay. Same caveat as other catch cards: a party member's catch broadcast can occasionally count (see icb-highland-shark-tracker).
